newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO firm but upside limited by supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO firm but upside limited by supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were expected to trade steady to firm on crude gains but the upside is limited as supplies were ample, traders said.
They said cash fundamentals remained bearish as one to two majors were heard to be high on stocks and some South Korean supplies remained unsold.
"The majors are unwilling to sell off their current inventories as they expected prices to edge higher," said a trader.
"Supplies from South Korea are also abundant and the Chinese are not taking very much," he said.
"Bids into China were seen at $127 per tonne," he said referring to cargoes on a cost-and-freight basis to south China for early November.
But most traders expected prices to firm. They said current fuel oil prices are still lagging behind the high crude oil and gas oil prices.
In the swaps market, November fuel oil was discussed at $120.75/$122, barely changed from Friday's quotes.
